chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Sufyan al-Jariri, from Abd al-Mumin al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Blessing consists of ten parts; nine-tenths of it are in commerce, and the remaining tenth is in skins.

The compiler of this book said, may God be pleased with him: By skins is meant sheep. Confirmation of this is what has been narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said: 'Nine-tenths of sustenance are in commerce and the remaining part is in the spoils (of war),' meaning sheep.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten parts of blessing according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the economic primacy of trade in Shia tradition, noting that nine-tenths of divine blessing (barakah) is concentrated in commerce, while the remaining tenth is attributed to livestock or war spoils. This narration underscores the spiritual legitimacy of mercantile activity as a primary means of sustenance, distinguishing it from other forms of wealth acquisition. The compiler’s clarification links the concept of 'skins' to sheep, reinforcing the tangible, agricultural basis of this tenth portion.
